newsitem.title: POLAND: Zywiec 1997 sales seen up 20-25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Zywiec 1997 sales seen up 20-25 pct.

text.p: Polish brewer Zywiec SA expects to lift its sales in 1997 by at least 20-25 percent from 265.7 million zlotys last year, the company's president said on Tuesday.
"The sales in 1997 should rise by 20-25 percent plus a part of inflation rate," Jean Francois van Boxmeer told Reuters during the company's general shareholders meeting.
Boxmeer said Zywiec wanted to sell two million hectolitres of beer in 1997, 300,000 hectolitres more than last year.
He added further increase was likely in 1998, but did not give details.
He also said the company was not planning in the immediate future to brew Heineken beer in Poland. Heineken is Zywiec's largest shareholder with a 31.8-percent stake.
Boxmeer also said Zywiec was not planning a new share issue.
